answer: Seeded Assignment by Delayed Cipher Draw: each epoch, a public randomness beacon derives a cipher key only after registration closes. New identities are assigned to verification slots via that keyed shuffle, so attackers cannot precompute which checks they will face. They must fund and maintain every account through unpredictable audit rounds, and repeated failures across randomly drawn slots raise per-identity cost until flooding an orchard of agents yields no cheap walnut of influence.
